title: Overview
body: NGP Table is a headless data table for Angular. You bring the markup and the styles; the table brings the state: sorting, filtering, grouping, selection, expansion and row editing, all as signals.

title: How the docs are organized
breadcrumb: Overview › How the docs are organized
body: Getting Started — what the table is and how a first table fits together. State Layer — createTable() and the with*() features that add behavior to it.

title: Introduction
body: NGP Table separates what a table knows from what it shows.

title: Three layers
body: State layer. createTable() returns a table instance that owns rows, columns and every feature's state as signals. Columns layer. columnSchema() declares per-column rules such as visibility. UI layer. Attribute directives like ngpTable and ngpTableCell connect your own markup to the state. They never insert, remove or reorder DOM.

title: Features compose as arguments
breadcrumb: 0. Getting Started › Introduction › Features compose as arguments
body: Each behavior is an opt-in feature passed to createTable() after the options object: A feature you do not pass is not in your bundle.

title: Sorting
body: withSorting() adds sorting to a table. The sort state is an ordered array of rules; an earlier rule takes priority over a later one.

title: Sort state
body: Each rule names a column and a direction, 'asc' or 'desc':

title: Methods
body: Method What it does toggleSort(id) Moves the column through ascending → descending → unsorted. setSorting(rules) Replaces the whole sort state. clearSorting() Removes every rule.

title: Multi-column sort
breadcrumb: 1. State Layer › Sorting › Methods › Multi-column sort
body: By default, toggleSort() on another column replaces the sort with that column alone. Pass multi: true to add each clicked column to the rules instead, in click order: setSorting() accepts any list of rules either way.

title: Server-side sorting
body: With manual: true, the table updates its sort state but does not sort rows itself. React to sortChanged with your own effect(), fetch sorted data, and write it to your data signal.

title: Per-column rules
body: Column-specific behavior goes in the schema option: sortFn sets the column's comparator. Without one, strings, numbers and dates compare automatically. sortable decides whether toggleSort() affects the column. Columns are sortable by default. sortNulls places null and empty values first or last.
